Ram Simgh And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 20
April, 2023
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 84
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 3746 of 2023
Applicant :- Ram Simgh And 2 Others

entities.text: Ram Simgh And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And Another Counsel for Applicant :- Pradeep Kumar Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Sanjay Kumar Pal Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
Supplementary affidavit filed by learned counsel for the accused-applicant today is taken on record.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

This application has been moved on behalf of the applicants 1. Ram Singh, 2. Bechan and 3. Anari Devi seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No.318 of 2019, under Sections 498-A, 304-B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Badhalganj, District- Gorakhpur.

It has been argued by the learned counsel for the applicants that applicants are innocent and they have apprehension of their arrest in the above-mentioned case, whereas there is no credible evidence against them.
Allegations levelled against the applicants are false.
The investigation of the case has been completed and charge-sheet has been filed and cognizance has been taken by the Court concerned.
Process under Sections 82 and 83 CrPC have also been issued against the applicants.
It has been submitted that in case applicants are granted anticipatory bail, they shall not misuse the liberty of bail and would obey all conditions of bail.

sentences.text: Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and submits that it is a case of dowry death wherein death was caused to the deceased Smt. Rani Nishad by her in-laws.
It is further submitted that although the accused applicants were named in the F.I.R., charge sheet was not filed against them.
During trial, they were summoned to face trial u/s 498-A, 304-B I.P.C. and Section 4 Dowry Prohibition Act on application u/s 319 Cr.P.C. by the Sessions court vide order dated 07.04.2022.
It is further submitted that post mortem report reveals that cause of death is ante-mortem injury and the hyoid bone is also fractured.
It is also submitted that the accused applicants are not entitled to grant anticipatory bail as the offence is very grievous in nature.
Learned counsel for the accused applicants has submitted that no offence evidence was collected against the present accused applicants and during the course of investigation.
Charge sheet has not been filed against them.

It is further submitted that the order passed by the trial court u/s 319 Cr.P.C. was challenged before this Court in Criminal Revision No.1972 of 2022 but the same was dismissed vide order dated 02.01.2023.
It is also submitted that a specific plea of separate living has been taken by the accused persons, who are the father-in-law, mother-in-law and Jeth of the deceased.
It is also prayed that they are entitled for grant of bail of anticipatory bail in this matter.

Keeping in view all the facts and circumstances of the case and also keeping into account the facts that P.W.1 Deepak Nishad-informant/brother of the deceased in his statement before the court has made specific allegations against the present accused applicants for their active participation in the alleged crime.
I do not find it a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail.

In Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1, the Hon'ble Apex Court has settled the controversy finally by holding the anticipatory bail need not be of limited duration invariably.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In appropriate case, it can continue upto conclusion of trial.
It has been further held therein that anticipatory bail granted can, depending on the conduct and behavior of the accused, continue after filing of the charge sheet till end of trial.

It has been further held by the Hon'ble Apex Court that while considering an application for grant of anticipatory bail, the court has to consider the nature of the offence, the role of the person, the likelihood of his influencing the course of investigation, or tampering with evidence including intimidating witnesses, llikelihood of fleeing justice, such as leaving the country, etc.

It has further been held that Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case, while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail, or refuse it.
Whether to grant or not is a matter of discretion.

It appears from a perusal of the record that in this matter since the applicants did not appear before the Court concerned despite issuance of process, punitive actions were taken against them, as they were absconding.
Processes under Sections 82 and 83 CrPC were issued against them.
The conduct of the applicants fall within the ambit of the law promulgated by Hon'ble Apex Court in Prem Shankar Prasad Versus State of Bihar and Another, 2021 SCC OnLine Supreme Court 955.

sentences.text: From the record, it reveals that the arrest warrant was issued by the Magistrate against the accused and thereafter proceedings under Sections 82, 83 Cr.P.C. had been initiated pursuant to the order passed by the Magistrate.
Only thereafter the accused moved an application before the trial court for anticipatory bail, which was rejected by the Sessions Court.
However, subsequently anticipatory bail was granted to the aforesaid accused by the High Court and when the matter came before the Hon'ble Apex Court, it was observed like this.

"19. Despite the above observations on merits and despite the fact that it was brought to the notice of the High Court that respondent No. 2 - accused is absconding and even the proceedings under sections 82-83 of Cr. P.C. have been initiated as far as back on 10.01.2019, the High Court has just ignored the aforesaid relevant aspects and has granted anticipatory bail to respondent No. 2 - accused by observing that the nature of accusation is arising out of a business transaction.
The specific allegations of cheating, etc., which came to be considered by learned Additional Sessions Judge has not at all been considered by the High Court.
Even the High Court has just ignored the factum of initiation of proceedings under sections 82-83 of Cr. P.C. by simply observing that "be that as it may".
The aforesaid relevant aspect on grant of anticipatory bail ought not to have been ignored by the High Court and ought to have been considered by the High Court very seriously and not casually.

20. In the case of State of Madhya Pradesh v. Pradeep Sharma (Supra), it is observed and held by this court that if anyone is declared as an absconder/proclaimed offender in terms of section 82 of Cr. P.C., he is not entitled to relief of anticipatory bail."

entities.text: State of Madhya Pradesh v. Pradeep Sharma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, I deem it not a fit case to grant anticipatory bail to the present applicants.
Such a person, who does not cooperate in the matter, is not entitled for any relief from this Court by way of granting anticipatory bail.
Prayer made in the application is refused.
The anticipatory bail application is rejected.
